purpose: Override evidence metadata for existing misconception records after targeted empirical review.

overrides.note: Operational-versus-relational equal-sign reasoning is directly supported in a Grades 3-5 study; no jurisdictional prevalence or item validation.
Whole-number digit-length interference is supported, but the verified school-age sample is Grade 7.
Empirical studies document area/perimeter difficulty; samples are local.
Grades 3-6 research documents inappropriate additive reasoning on proportional problems; not every ratio error has this cause.
Broader graph-interpretation evidence does not directly establish the exact scale-assumed-one error.

A two-student Grades 5-7 case study documents a robust repeated-addition/equal-groups conception that constrained later reasoning; a Year 2 intervention found stronger multiplicative-reasoning gains from correspondence-schema teaching. Do not diagnose from strategy use or claim prevalence.

An X0X zero-omission error such as 504→54 is directly documented in the Kuwaiti/Arabic-speaking sample but absent in the comparable English sample. Probe locally rather than generalising to Chinese-speaking pupils.
Direct research supports side-length interference in angle-size judgement; retain age/sample limits.
Second-grade experiments support difficulty understanding ruler units as spatial intervals, especially on shifted-start tasks.
Middle-school design research supports the structural rationale but not primary-pupil prevalence or every exact conversion error.
Direct Grades 2/4 evidence supports hand-specific difficulty and hour-minute relational reasoning, but not the exact same-scale wording.
Direct Grades 2-5 evidence supports hierarchical hour-minute unit coordination as a major elapsed-time difficulty, not every exact endpoint-subtraction error.

Year 3/4 interview research and national assessment evidence show calendar/time calculation difficulties, including adding days/weeks/years to dates. The study does not isolate assuming equal month lengths as the exact cause, so retain this wording as a probe hypothesis.

NFER assessment response data directly show KS1 difficulty distinguishing coin value from surface/notation cues, while established primary guidance targets unitising and total value. The exact number-of-coins-versus-total-value wording is retained as an instructional probe rather than a research-established prevalence claim.

Primary interview research directly supports subtraction-as-difference as a meaningful and variably accessible reasoning structure. It is not a money-specific misconception study, so the change wording remains a probe supported by the broader subtraction mechanism.
Grade 6 evidence directly documents surface-area/volume confusion; no universal prevalence claim.
Grade 6 constructed responses directly support formula/unit errors in volume measurement; no universal prevalence claim.

Kindergarten spinner-game research directly documents difficulty coordinating sector size with fairness/chance; Chinese Grade 5 research supports probability-comparison misconceptions more broadly. Do not infer prevalence or diagnose from one response.

resolver_rule: After resolving aliases, merge overrides by canonical misconception_id; evidence status/level supersede catalog metadata and source IDs are appended/deduplicated.
